title: Maximal tori of a semisimple Lie centralizer are ambient maximal tori
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All groups are affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and geometric connectedness have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $G$ be smooth and geometrically connected. A torus is a group becoming $\mathbf G_m^r$ over an algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], where $r\geq0$ and $\mathbf G_m(R)=R^\times$ [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type, def-sc-gm-ga]. A maximal torus is maximal among closed torus subgroups [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]. For a smooth group $J$ put $\mathfrak j=\operatorname{Lie}(J)=T_{J/k,e}$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], with its commutator Lie bracket [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Fix a faithful closed linear representation $i:G\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Call $X\in\mathfrak g$ semisimple if $di(X)$ is diagonalizable over $\bar k$, and noncentral if $[X,Y]\ne0$ for some $Y\in\mathfrak g$. Let $X\in\mathfrak g$ be semisimple. Write $K=C_G(X)^\circ$ for the identity component of the adjoint stabilizer $C_G(X)(R)=\{g\in G(R):\operatorname{Ad}(g)(X\otimes1)=X\otimes1\}$, where $\operatorname{Ad}$ is the differential of conjugation. Then every maximal $k$-torus of $K$ is a maximal $k$-torus of $G$. This includes central $X$ and $X=0$, and assumes neither reductivity nor perfectness.

source.place: Proposition 17.90 and its proof, printed p.381, restricted to the identity component of the adjoint stabilizer; maximal tori lie in that component. The case X=0 is immediate.

proof.text: Put $H=C_G(X)$. By [lem-sfb-semisimple-tangent-stabilizer], $H$ is smooth and closed and $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\{Y:[Y,X]=0\}$, so $X\in\operatorname{Lie}(H)$. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-group-identity-subgroup], $K=H^\circ$ is an open and closed connected subgroup; it is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. The dual-number point of $X$ has its only underlying point at the identity, hence factors through this open $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. Thus $X\in\operatorname{Lie}(K)$. Fix a maximal $k$-torus $T\subseteq K$ and put $F=\bar k$. The group $K_F$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] (2), and connected by [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected], applied to $K$ with its identity section. By [lem-sfb-maximal-torus-field-extension], $T_F$ is maximal in $K_F$. The natural scalar-extension tangent isomorphisms in [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus] give $X_F\in\operatorname{Lie}(K_F)$; the base-changed faithful matrix of $X_F$ is diagonalizable by hypothesis. Every $T_F$-point fixes $X_F$, since $T\subseteq H$ as subgroup schemes.

source.place: Proposition 17.90, printed p.381, first sentence; Proposition 17.76, p.377; Proposition 1.34, pp.16–17; Theorem 17.82, p.379. Scalar extension is used only to obtain the Cartan product over the perfect field F.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-neutral-torus-centralizer-cartan-structure] to the smooth connected $F$-group $K_F$ and its maximal torus $T_F$. Write $D=C_{K_F}(T_F)$ and $C=D^\circ$. This provides smooth connected $C$ and a smooth connected unipotent subgroup $U$ with multiplication $U\times_F T_F\simeq C$ an isomorphism of group schemes. We verify $X_F\in\operatorname{Lie}(C)$ using whole-torus invariance, not just Lie-algebra invariance. In the notation of [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus], for every $F$-algebra $R$ and $t\in T_F(R)$ one has
$$tE_{K_F,R}(X_F\otimes1)t^{-1}=E_{K_F,R}(\operatorname{Ad}(t)(X_F\otimes1))=E_{K_F,R}(X_F\otimes1).$$
For an $F[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$-algebra $R$, specialize the displayed equality along $R[\delta]/\delta^2\to R$, $\delta\mapsto\epsilon_R$. Naturality shows that the image of $E_{K_F,F}(X_F)$ commutes with every $t\in T_F(R)$. This is exactly membership in $D(F[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2)$. Its underlying point is the identity, so it factors through the open $C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. Consequently $X_F\in\operatorname{Lie}(C)$.

source.place: Proposition 17.90, printed p.381, Cartan subgroup and its tangent vector; Proposition 17.28, p.360; Theorem 16.47 and Corollary 16.48, p.341. The dual-number calculation spells out the fixed-vector assertion.

proof.text: Let $p:C\to U$ be the projection from the product in step 2. By [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-unitriangular-embedding], choose a closed immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_m\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_{m,F}$ into upper unitriangular matrices. Its hypotheses hold: $U$ is smooth and its unipotence is precisely geometric unipotence in a faithful representation, as supplied by the Cartan structure node. The restricted embedding $i_F|_C$ is faithful and closed, and its differential at $X_F$ is the given diagonalizable matrix. Apply the arbitrary-field representation clause of [lem-sfb-algebraic-lie-additive-jordan] to $C$, this embedding, and the representation $j\circ p$. It says that $A=d(j\circ p)(X_F)$ is diagonalizable. On the other hand the dual-number formula $I_m+\epsilon A$ from [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus] lies in $\mathcal U_m(F[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2)$, so $A$ is strictly upper triangular. Thus $A^m=0$; in a diagonalizing basis every eigenvalue has $m$th power zero and hence is zero. Therefore $A=0$. Functoriality of differentials and injectivity of $dj$, in the same Lie/Jordan nodes, imply $dp(X_F)=0$. Taking dual-number points in $C\simeq U\times_F T_F$ identifies tangent vectors with pairs and $dp$ with their first projection. Its kernel is therefore exactly $\operatorname{Lie}(T_F)$, proving $X_F\in\operatorname{Lie}(T_F)$.

source.place: Proposition 17.90, printed p.381, the inference from the unipotent quotient to X in Lie(T), made explicit with the product over F; Example 17.75 and Proposition 17.74, p.377; Theorem 14.5, pp.281–282.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus], the inclusion $\operatorname{Lie}(T)\subseteq\mathfrak g$ becomes the inclusion $\operatorname{Lie}(T_F)\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(G_F)$ after scalar extension. Extend a $k$-basis of the former subspace to a basis of $\mathfrak g$. The coordinates of $X_F$ outside that subspace are the images in $F$ of the corresponding coordinates of $X$. Step 3 makes all of them zero, and $k\to F$ is injective. Thus $X\in\operatorname{Lie}(T)$.

source.place: Proposition 17.90, printed p.381, X in Lie(T); elementary faithful-field descent of subspace membership using tangent scalar extension, Section 10.19, pp.191–192.

proof.text: Let $S\subseteq G$ be any $k$-torus containing $T$. It is smooth and connected by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus]. It is commutative: the comultiplication of $\mathcal O(S)$ and its composite with the swap agree after $-\otimes_k\bar k$, since $S_{\bar k}\cong\mathbf G_m^r$ is commutative, and $\mathcal O(S)\otimes_k\mathcal O(S)\to(\mathcal O(S)\otimes_k\mathcal O(S))\otimes_k\bar k$ is injective. Commutativity of $S$ implies that every $s\in S(R)$ centralizes every infinitesimal point from $\operatorname{Lie}(S)\otimes_kR$ after every $k$-algebra extension. Since $X\in\operatorname{Lie}(T)\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(S)$, the conjugation identity and subgroup compatibility of [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus] give $\operatorname{Ad}(s)(X\otimes1)=X\otimes1$ for all $R,s$. The defining stabilizer functor therefore gives a homomorphism $S\to H$ whose composite with $H\hookrightarrow G$ is the given inclusion. The underlying image of connected $S$ is connected and contains the identity, so lies in $K=H^\circ$. As $K$ is open, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] gives a factorization $S\to K$; the original closed inclusion into $G$ is still a closed inclusion into $K$ (on affine coordinate algebras, its quotient map factors through the quotient defining $K$). Hence $S$ is a torus subgroup of $K$ containing $T$. Maximality of $T$ in $K$ forces $S=T$. This is maximality of $T$ in $G$. No step required $X\ne0$ or noncentrality.

source.place: Proposition 17.90, printed p.381, final two sentences, using an arbitrary containing k-torus instead of first choosing an ambient maximal torus.
